vo: Picture a company run by one person and a crew of Bots. No office full of staff. Just one founder, deciding what matters.
A business that once needed twenty people can now run on a founder, a couple of part-timers, and Bots handling the routine work.
Here's the plan. Find a problem worth solving, then build four Bots in a smart order, and finally connect them to one shared brain.
Start with the mistake most people make: building before choosing the pain. Sell a painkiller, not a vitamin. People pay fast to stop pain.
Ask your Bot for fifty real problems in your market. Then keep the three that people are already paying to fix.
Message ten of them, and don't pitch. Ask for advice. Advice becomes a call, and a call becomes your first customer.
Once customers arrive, your time vanishes. So automate in order, climbing one rung at a time. The first rung is your inbox.
Every Bot needs four ingredients. Your own data, a playbook to follow, a schedule, and a signal that tells you it's working.
For the inbox, your data is your sent mail. Tell the Bot to read every reply you wrote, find your rules, and sort new mail the same way.
Add a playbook for your calendar. Your working hours, your deep work time, your home time. Then every request lands in the right slot.
Now close the loop. The Bot drafts, you edit and send, then it compares its draft with your final and updates its rules. Without that loop, it's not an agent.
Schedule it twice a day. And add a signal: a short message with your drafts, and who still hasn't replied. Start in review mode, and let go slowly.
Rung two is delivery. The moment someone pays, a Bot sends the welcome, collects the intake form, sets up the client folder, and aims for a first win that same day.
To teach it, just talk. Have the Bot interview you, one question at a time, then list every step and mark which ones really need you.
Your signal here is a client board. Green, yellow, red, and how long each person has been stuck. You only fix the red ones.
Rung three is marketing, and it comes after delivery on purpose. New customers only help if you can look after them properly.
Use your best customers as the pattern. Each morning, the Bot finds ten new people like them, and brings them to you with where they're talking about the problem.
It can also draft short video scripts in your voice, based on real, specific problems. If the topics feel generic, ask for something more precise.
Watch the whole funnel. How many leads it found, how many were qualified, booked, and bought. Then feed the winners back in.
The last rung is sales. The close stays human. The Bot handles everything around it: qualifying, follow-ups, rebooking no-shows, and updating your records.
Start with coaching. The Bot plays your ideal buyer, you practice, and it scores how much you talked, which steps you skipped, and which objections tripped you up.
Track your win rate, and keep the records clean, so delivery never has to ask the client the same question twice.
But right now each Bot works alone. Give them one shared brain. Your mail, calendar, calls, customer records and documents, all in one place.
Begin with a single handoff. On Friday, sales saves the top objections. On Monday, marketing turns them into next week's topics.
There's one thing a Bot can't do, and that's choosing where you're heading. The vision stays yours. Hand the rest over.
So find the painkiller, climb the ladder, and share one brain. This week, start with the inbox.
